description.text: A gives B a five-second lead in a 1200 meter race, yet A wins by five seconds. Even when A gives C a 10-second head start in the identical race, A still wins by a 10-second margin. In the same race, by how many seconds will B win if B gives C a five-second head start?

properties.html: A gives B a five-second lead in a 1200 meter race, yet A wins by five seconds. Even when A gives C a 10-second head start in the identical race, A still wins by a 10-second margin. In the same race, by how many seconds will B win if B gives C a five-second head start?

questionFeedback:
Sorry, that's not correct.
Explanation:

Let, A completes the race in t seconds
So, B completes the race in (t+10) seconds
So, C completes the race in (t+20) seconds
Now, B gives C a 5 seconds head start, so C needs (t+20-5) = (t+15)seconds to complete the race.
But B needs (t+10) seconds to complete the race. Therefore, B will win by = (t+15-t-10) = 5 seconds.
